name: NextEra Energy Resources (NEER)
employees: NEE total ~17,300 (Dec 2025, 10-K); NEER-only headcount not disclosed

ownership.notes: NEER is the competitive-energy arm of NextEra Energy (~$300B enterprise value, ~80 GW operating company-wide), sister to regulated utility FPL. A $67B merger with Dominion Energy was announced May 18, 2026 (close expected 2H 2027) — it would create the world's largest regulated electric utility and hand NextEra the Virginia data-center alley.

summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: NextEra Energy Resources is the largest storage demand signal in the United States and the anchor customer of the NON-Chinese supply chain. It operates ~5.2 GW of battery storage, placed >2 GW in service in 2025 alone, holds a storage backlog of roughly 11-13 GWh inside a 35.1 GW signed renewables+storage backlog, and discloses a 95 GW standalone/co-located storage expansion pipeline. It buys as a self-integrator — cells and DC blocks direct from manufacturers, no Tesla/Fluence channel — and has locked 'competitively priced domestic battery supply secured through 2029' at 1.5x inventory coverage, 'expected to be FEOC compliant' (Samsung SDI is the confirmed piece, ~6.3 GWh reported; the master domestic counterparty remains undisclosed). Its AIDC franchise is unmatched: a Google partnership co-developing gigawatt-scale data-center campuses (15 GW by 2035 base case, 30-35 GW upside), ~2.5 GW of Meta PPAs including two storage ESAs, the Duane Arnold nuclear restart under a 25-yr Google PPA, 9.5 GW of US-Japan gas, and the pending Dominion merger. For a §154-named Chinese OEM, NEER's ITC-qualifying pipeline is effectively closed through decade-end — this dossier exists because NextEra defines the market everyone else sells into.
ecosystemRole: We assess NEER as the market-maker rather than a realistic account: it sets the price and speed benchmarks (storage buildable in 16-18 months vs 4-5 years for gas peakers — Ketchum's core pitch to hyperscalers), it anchors the domestic cell industry's demand (its 2026-2029 needs are covered at 1.5x by non-FEOC supply, making it the pillar customer for Korean/US cell capacity), and it is the single largest AIDC energy counterparty — a position the Dominion merger would extend into the world's largest data-center market. The relationship-web read: every IPP in this batch competes with NEER for hyperscaler dollars, every domestic cell maker leans on its order book, and its procurement doctrine (self-integration + long-dated domestic locks + vendor-borne tariff risk) is the template other large buyers copy. The one scenario that could reopen procurement to outsiders: a production slip at its concentrated domestic supplier base.

productsAndServices.name: Storage development & operating platform
productsAndServices.description: ~5.2 GW NEER operating battery storage (Dec 2025; NEE-wide 6.17 GW incl. FPL's 991 MW); >2 GW placed in service in 2025 (+~220% YoY); storage ≈ one-third of the ~30-35 GW signed backlog; 95 GW standalone + co-located storage expansion pipeline (company-claimed, Jan 2026). Named projects: North Dakota 100 MW/400 MWh (approved Apr 2026); Meta ESAs in New Mexico (168 MW storage, CODs 2026-2028); Lock Energy Center CA (500 MW total; OCPA 115 MW/460 MWh 20-yr ESA with explicit tariff/'federal action' cost-sharing protections); Dominguez UT (200 MW, ~$128.6M, COD Dec 2026); Southwest Atlanta GA (250 MW/1,000 MWh); Corby CA (300 MW/1,200 MWh, filed with CEC to bypass a local moratorium); pursuing 8-hour durations.
productsAndServices.positioning: The largest storage builder-owner in the US; Wood Mackenzie/ESN coverage (Jul 2026) noted NextEra entering the top ranks of integrator league tables despite being a developer — because it self-integrates.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Utility tolls/ESAs (SRP-class 20-yr structures, OCPA, TVA-style), hyperscaler ESAs (Meta — storage contracted directly with a hyperscaler), merchant + hedges; funded on balance sheet + tax-credit transfers.
productsAndServices.roadmap: 4-hr → 8-hr duration push (Ketchum, Q2 2026); storage framed as 'the only new capacity resource available at scale' this decade.

productsAndServices.name: Procurement machine (self-integration + domestic locks)
productsAndServices.description: NextEra buys cells/DC blocks and BOP components directly and integrates in-house. Confirmed: Samsung SDI — contract signed Mar 2025 (first tranche ~$301M; Korean-press-reported ~6.3 GWh total across projects; 20-ft Samsung Battery Box). Disclosed but unnamed: a master 'US-made batteries' contract (revealed Jan 2025) structured so domestic-content ITC adders offset residual tariff cost, with tariff risk borne by the supplier. Stated position (repeated through Q2 2026): domestic battery supply secured through 2029 at 1.5x inventory coverage vs development expectations, 'expected to be FEOC compliant'; battery tariff exposure 'negligible.' Balance of plant equally locked: switchgear/breakers through 2029, transformers through 2030, solar panels through 2029 at 1.5x.
productsAndServices.positioning: The FEOC playbook executed at maximum scale: begin-construction-by-Dec-31-2025 exemptions banked for the near-term backlog; credits underwritten through ~2030. No verified CATL master agreement exists (the recurring 'CATL 2,400 MWh Utah' claim traces to a single low-quality aggregator — unverified); no Hithium history of any kind found.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct OEM/cell supply agreements; centralized Integrated Supply Chain organization.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Internal fleet supply at ~5 GW/yr of storage origination.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Concentration is the watch item: one undisclosed master supplier plus Samsung SDI covering 2026-2029 means a Korean/US LFP production slip is the single scenario that could reopen procurement.

productsAndServices.name: AIDC energy franchise ('energy pragmatism')
productsAndServices.description: All-of-the-above seller to hyperscalers: renewables+storage as the speed-to-market first phase of a campus, then gas and nuclear layered in. Google partnership (Dec 2025): co-developing gigawatt-scale data-center campuses (first three in development), 15 GW of new generation for data-center hubs by 2035 base / 30-35 GW upside, plus a technology leg (Google Cloud AI for NextEra's 'Rewire'; NextEra receives SaaS revenue). Meta (Dec 2025): ~2.5 GW via 11 PPAs + 2 storage ESAs. Duane Arnold 615 MW nuclear restart (Q1 2029, $1.6B+, 25-yr Google PPA); Point Beach/Seabrook recontracting; 6 GW of SMR site opportunities. Gas: GE Vernova framework with turbine slots for 4 GW CCGT; >20 GW gas pipeline; 9.5 GW in TX+PA selected under the US-Japan $550B investment vehicle (Mar 2026). 20+ potential hubs (Jan 2026) → 30+ (Apr 2026), targeting ~40 by YE 2026; >10.5 GW already serving tech/data-center customers.
productsAndServices.positioning: The only IPP with a Google-scale co-development framework, a restart nuclear asset under hyperscaler PPA, a federal gas mandate, and (post-Dominion) the world's largest data-center utility territory. Ketchum prices gas at $2,600-2,800/kW and 6+ year timelines — storage stays the speed lever inside its own stack.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Hub co-development, PPAs/ESAs, full-requirements Customer Supply unit (firm gas procurement, hedging).
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Hyperscalers (Google, Meta), utilities facing large-load growth (Xcel alliance), federal/bilateral programs.
productsAndServices.roadmap: FPL side: 20+ GW of large-load inquiries, ~9 GW in paid interconnection studies, service from 2028, ~$2B capex per GW; Dominion merger closes 2H 2027 if approved.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess NEER as structurally closed to §154-named Chinese suppliers through decade-end: domestic supply locked through 2029 at 1.5x coverage and 'expected to be FEOC compliant', safe-harbored begin-construction positions covering the near-term backlog, ITC economics that cannot tolerate prohibited-foreign-entity content, and (post-Dominion) a regulated-majority profile that is even more politically domestic-biased. This account is a market force to plan around, not a target to sell into.

(High confidence) We assess the self-integration model as the second structural barrier: NextEra buys cells and DC blocks direct and integrates in-house, so a containerized-system vendor has no integrator channel to ride — the only entry point is direct cell/DC-block supply, exactly where FEOC math bites hardest.

(Moderate confidence) We assess supplier concentration as the one reopening scenario: 2026-2029 demand covered by Samsung SDI plus one undisclosed master supplier means a Korean/US LFP ramp slip would force NextEra back into the market mid-decade — a low-probability, high-value contingency worth monitoring via Samsung SDI/LGES US production news.

(High confidence) We assess NEER as the defining AIDC energy counterparty: the Google co-development framework (15-35 GW), Meta's 2.5 GW with direct storage ESAs, Duane Arnold, the US-Japan gas mandate, and ~40 targeted hubs collectively set the terms every other IPP in this batch competes against. For Hithium's market model, NextEra's hub economics (storage at 16-18 months as phase one of a campus) is the demand thesis that justifies the whole US containerized-BESS opportunity — captured by whoever can supply FEOC-compliant hardware.

(Moderate confidence) For the Hithium lens: treat NEER as intelligence, not pipeline — track its earnings-call supply-chain language as the best public indicator of domestic-supply tightness, its hub count as the AIDC demand curve, and the Dominion approval process (VA/NC/SC politics, FPL scandal history resurfacing Aug 2026) as the timeline for the largest utility procurement machine in the country changing hands.

relationships.note: Landmark co-development framework: gigawatt-scale DC campuses (15 GW by 2035 base, 30-35 GW upside) + the Duane Arnold nuclear restart under a 25-year Google PPA.

December 2025: NextEra and Google agreed to co-develop gigawatt-scale data-center campuses — first three in development, 15 GW of new generation for data-center hubs by 2035 base case with 30-35 GW upside — plus a technology leg (Google Cloud AI powering NextEra's 'Rewire'; NextEra receives SaaS revenue).

Behind it sits the Duane Arnold 615 MW nuclear restart (Q1 2029, $1.6B+) under a 25-year Google PPA — nuclear restarts monetized through hyperscaler offtake, the premium tier of the AIDC energy stack.

relationships.context: Announced the same day as the Google framework (Dec 8, 2025): Meta signed ~2.5 GW with NEER — 11 PPAs plus two energy storage agreements including 168 MW of New Mexico storage with CODs 2026-2028. The dossier's marker: storage contracted DIRECTLY with a hyperscaler in ESA format — proof NextEra sells storage as an AIDC product, not just an ITC asset.

relationships.note: Confirmed multi-project ESS supply — first tranche ~$301M, reported ~6.3 GWh of 20-ft Samsung Battery Boxes.
relationships.context: March 2025: Samsung SDI confirmed a multi-project ESS supply deal with NextEra (first tranche ~$301M; Korean-press-reported ~6.3 GWh total). It is the one named piece of NEER's domestic-supply wall — 'competitively priced domestic battery supply secured through 2029' at 1.5x inventory coverage, with the master domestic counterparty still undisclosed. NEER buys as a self-integrator: cells and DC blocks direct, no Tesla/Fluence channel.

One of the two supply walls — gas turbines and domestic cells — locked years forward against the AIDC demand wave.
